item.title: Best Practices for Secure String Encryption and Authentication in PHP
item.description:
“Best Practices for Secure String Encryption and Authentication in PHP”

When dealing with data protection, what is the proper sequence for applying encryption and authentication? How can developers leverage modern cryptographic tools in PHP to ensure data integrity and confidentiality, avoiding common pitfalls like using insecure modes or rolling custom crypto?

The Crucial Difference: Encryption vs. Authenticated Encryption

A fundamental aspect of robust security is grasping the distinction between simple encryption and Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD). You almost certainly require authenticated encryption, not just confidentiality via encryption alone.

item.title: C# AES Encryption: Secure Data Transformation Methods Explained
item.description:
“C# AES Encryption: Secure Data Transformation Methods Explained”

How can we effectively implement two-way encryption in C# applications, particularly focusing on secure algorithms like AES, while addressing concerns like URL compatibility and proper key/IV management? Various approaches exist, leveraging the System.Security.Cryptography namespace to handle cryptographic operations.

Here we examine several implementations provided by experts, comparing their structure, security considerations, and utility for web contexts.

Approach 1: Basic AES Implementation with Custom URL Encoding (SimpleAES)

One foundational approach utilizes RijndaelManaged (the underlying engine for AES in older frameworks) and includes custom methods to serialize byte arrays into URL-safe strings and back.
